messages:
maria: Quick report from a new hire onboarding - JS sample app shows duplicated tail tokens when the dev hits reconnect quickly after ctrl-c.

alex: Rough repro steps?

maria: Start streaming, interrupt (ctrl-c) during a chunk, then immediately reconnect (within ~100-300ms). Node SDK v0.9.1. Outcome: sometimes the last token is emitted twice or a short fragment appears out of order.

ryan: Sounds like our reconnect path replaying a buffered write while resume metadata also gets applied. We debounce buffer flushes for 50ms which can hide this.

sam: Any difference in python?

maria: Python less flaky because its parser treats lines atomically; JS uses delimiter parsing and the abort can truncate the delimiter.

alex: Can you paste the curl minimal repro so others can try?

maria: Sure:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"edge reconnect test"}'
```

ci-bot: CI run 4832 attached: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/4832 (streaming-e2e flaky)

ryan: Two actionable leads: 1) server include per-chunk seq numbers in resume metadata so clients can dedupe; 2) SDK should emit a clear "resume_complete" event with last-seq. Also consider immediate buffer flush on teardown (skip debounce).

sam: I'll add a sample-app flag to emulate fast reconnects and include a tiny dedupe helper snippet. Also add a node/python parity test for abort+auth-refresh.

maria: Temp workaround for docs: advise 200-300ms reconnect backoff and bump keepalive to 30s in sample app. Not perfect but reduces hit rate for new users.

alex: Create an internal issue and add to onboarding checklist. Prioritize small SDK event patch and server seq header.
maria: Filed: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-3180

alex: Great, thanks. :thumbsup:
